ideas.title: Encode semantic-boundary uncertainty as an explicit SID token
ideas.motivation: Items with noisy, sparse, or ambiguous content embeddings can receive brittle codes; a recommender that treats these codes as equally certain may overfit accidental distinctions and miss useful alternatives.
ideas.novelty: Rather than changing the embedding geometry or adding another interaction-transition loss, measure how stable each item's quantized code is under train-only perturbations and expose that stability in its identifier.
ideas.key_change: Generate several perturbed views of each training item embedding, quantize each with the trained codebooks, and append a small stability token to the ordinary SID. The token summarizes agreement, allowing the generative recommender to learn when a semantic code should be interpreted coarsely versus confidently.
ideas.specification: For each item i with embedding x_i, form B train-only perturbations x_i^(b)=x_i+epsilon^(b), epsilon^(b)~N(0,sigma^2 diag(v)), where v is the per-dimension variance estimated over training-item embeddings. Quantize each view with the frozen baseline quantizer to obtain tuple q_i^(b). Let a_i=(1/B) max_q sum_b 1[q_i^(b)=q]. Assign stability token s_i= min(S-1, floor(S*a_i)), with S=4 bins (use bins [0,.5), [.5,.75), [.75,.95), [.95,1]); export SID_i=(q_i,s_i). Keep perturbations and all statistics fit using training items only; apply identical deterministic seeded perturbations at export. Compare against baseline at fixed sequence model and training budget.
ideas.cost_estimate: One additional batched quantization pass of B=8 per item; no codebook or recommender training cost change beyond the extra token vocabulary. Expected Stage2 wall time roughly 1.1–1.3x, dominated by quantization.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: On held-out next-item evaluation, adding s_i improves Recall@K/NDCG@K over the same baseline SID, with the largest gain among items whose bootstrap agreement a_i is low; verify by overall metrics and predeclared agreement-bin slices. Reject if gains are absent or confined to one unstable random seed.
ideas.risks: Embedding perturbations may not reflect real metadata noise; a stability token may just encode item frequency/popularity indirectly or consume sequence-model capacity. Hard agreement can be sensitive to sigma and codebook boundaries, and appended tokens may not be consumed usefully.

ideas.title: Add a compact train-only demand-shape suffix
ideas.motivation: Content-near items can have very different roles in user activity: some are repeatedly revisited while others are typically one-off discoveries. A content-only SID can therefore fail to distinguish items whose consumption patterns call for different continuation predictions.
ideas.novelty: This adds a low-cardinality behavioral descriptor derived from the shape of training-only item usage, not a transition/adjacency objective, graph embedding, or popularity-weighted codebook loss; the existing content SID remains unchanged.
ideas.key_change: Append a discretized demand-shape suffix computed from training interactions, separating repeat/revisit propensity from raw item frequency so the generative model can condition on distinct usage regimes without changing item embeddings.
ideas.specification: Using training sequences only, for each item i compute f_i=count of occurrences, u_i=count of distinct training users, and r_i=(number of users with >=2 occurrences of i)/(u_i+1). Compute p_i=log(1+f_i/u_i) (set to 0 if u_i=0). Within each training-only frequency decile, quantile-bin r_i into 3 bins; independently quantile-bin p_i into 2 bins. Append suffix d_i=6*b_r+b_p to the baseline SID. Fit decile boundaries and quantiles on training items/interactions only; freeze them for validation/test. Evaluate against the unmodified baseline using the same sequence split and model settings.
ideas.cost_estimate: Negligible: one pass over training interactions and a 12-token suffix vocabulary; no additional embedding model or quantizer training. Sequence-model cost is effectively unchanged.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The suffix improves held-out next-item ranking over baseline, especially for repeat-consuming users and within frequency-matched item groups; measure overall Recall@K/NDCG@K and those predeclared slices. It is not worth keeping if frequency-matched performance does not improve, indicating the suffix only duplicates popularity.
ideas.risks: Repeat propensity is noisy for infrequent items, and per-frequency-bin quantiles may be unstable; user/item leakage can arise if boundaries accidentally use validation or test interactions. The appended behavior may be nonstationary or redundant with sequence context and could worsen cold-item generalization.
